To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a combination of composition and process parameters can result in spray-dried powders with high fine particle fractions (21-41%) and a physical environment (gel phase of phospholipid) that is favorable to protein stability (albumin protected lactose).
a proper combination of spray-drying parameters, powder composition and airflow rate allows for the preparation of dry protein powders with elevated FPFs and a favorable physical environment.

the combination of composition and process parameters allows to obtain dry powder formulations of spray-dried aerosols with elevated fine particle fraction and physical environment favorable to the protein stability.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of dry powders for inhalation with improved aerosolization properties, a surface enriched with the lipophilic component DPPC and a protein stabilizing environment, which should facilitate the delivery of proteins to the lungs.
the development of inhalation powders with improved aerosolization properties and a favorable physical environment for protein stability.
the design of inhalation powders with improved aerodynamic properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a protein-stabilizing agent, such as a sugar or a sugar alcohol, in combination with the use of a surfactant, such as DPPC, is a promising approach for spray-dried protein formulations.
the combination of a protein, a phospholipid and a stabilizing sugar can lead to a dry powder aerosol with a high FPF and a favorable environment for protein stability.
the spray-dried protein powder is a complex system with a surface composition and physical structure that are different from the bulk powder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FPFs of spray-dried powders are determined by the bulk powder properties, i.e. particle size, particle size distribution, tap density, and particle surface properties.
a protein-lipid-sugar system is a promising candidate for inhalation of protein drugs.
spray-dried protein-lipid-polyol powders can be prepared with high FPFs and a physical state that may be suitable for pulmonary protein delivery.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the surface composition of protein powders prepared by spray-dryer is not necessarily representative of the bulk composition, which may have important consequences in terms of powder aerosolization behavior and protein stability.
protein powders can be produced with FPFs > 40% by using a combination of protein and sugar stabilizers and a proper spray-drying process.
protein powders can be designed to have high FPFs without compromising the physical state of the protein.
